title: Rigorous existence and location of quantum phase transitions in lattice Hamiltonian systems
abstract: We extend the analysis of the class of quantum phase transitions (QPTs) that can be interpreted as condensations in state space, first introduced in [M. Ostilli and C. Presilla, J. Phys. A 54, 055005 (2021)], by generalizing the arguments of [M. Ostilli and C. Presilla, Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 040601 (2021)] to prove the existence and determine the location (via simple bounds) of QPTs in general one-parameter lattice Hamiltonians. Unlike our original formulation, this extension also encompasses second-order QPTs, for which we provide the explicit example of the transverse-field Ising model. Our analysis suggests that, under conditions typically satisfied in physical contexts, any QPT taking place in lattice systems can be interpreted as a condensation in state space.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to prove the existence and locate Quantum Phase Transitions (QPTs) in lattice Hamiltonians. It achieves this by interpreting the transition as a condensation in state space, analyzing the ground-state energy in the thermodynamic limit. The work generalizes previous results, confirming applicability to second-order transitions and providing general bounds for the critical point.
main_problem: To rigorously prove the existence and determine the location of Quantum Phase Transitions (QPTs) in general one-parameter lattice Hamiltonian systems.
main_result: The analysis establishes that any QPT in lattice systems can be interpreted as a condensation in state space, and provides methods to rigorously bound the critical point $g_c$. The theory also demonstrates the possibility of multiple second-order crossings.
method: The approach involves decomposing the Hilbert space into two orthogonal subspaces and analyzing the ground-state energy per particle in the Thermodynamic Limit. The critical point is found where the energies from these two subspaces become equal.
model_or_system: The study focuses on lattice Hamiltonian systems described by $H = K + gV$, where $K$ and $V$ are non-commuting operators and $g$ is the tuning parameter. The analysis is general, applying to various lattice models.
key_observables: The primary observables are the ground-state energies per particle, $\epsilon_{	ext{cond}}(g)$ and $\epsilon_{	ext{norm}}(g)$, whose crossing determines the critical point $g_c$.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $g$, the critical point $g_c$, and the parameters defining the bounds $g_{\pm c}$ are crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a well-defined ground-state energy in the Thermodynamic Limit and relies on the concavity of the energy functions. The method also requires the ability to choose appropriate subspaces.
figures_summary: Figures sketch scenarios illustrating the possibility of multiple first-order and second-order QPTs occurring at different critical points.
paper_structure: The paper builds from extending previous work by interpreting QPTs as state-space condensations. It develops mathematical machinery using subspace decomposition and the Thermodynamic Limit to find bounds on $g_c$. Finally, it uses theoretical constructions (Appendix A) to demonstrate the possibility of multiple critical points.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting QPTs to state-space condensation provides a powerful, general diagnostic tool for identifying and locating phase transitions in complex quantum many-body systems.
